stem: A client asks a HIPAA-covered hospital for an electronic copy of protected health information (PHI) in a designated record set that the hospital maintains electronically. Which response by the nurse best reflects the client’s HIPAA right of access?

options.A: The hospital may provide only a paper copy whenever paper is easier for staff to produce.
options.B: The client generally may receive an electronic copy in a requested readily producible format, subject to limited grounds for denial.
options.C: The client must explain why the records are needed before an electronic copy can be released.
options.D: Electronic access is optional under HIPAA and depends entirely on the hospital’s internal policy.

rationale: B is correct. Under 45 CFR §164.524, individuals generally have a right to access PHI about themselves in a designated record set. When the PHI is maintained electronically, the individual generally has a right to an electronic copy; if the requested electronic form and format are readily producible, the covered entity must provide that form and format, and otherwise must provide a readable alternative electronic format agreed to by the individual and covered entity, subject to the limited grounds for denial in §164.524(a). A is incorrect because a covered entity generally cannot substitute paper merely because it is easier when an electronic copy is required and a readily producible electronic format is available. C is incorrect because an individual is not required to state a purpose for exercising the right of access. D is incorrect because the access right arises from HIPAA and is not left entirely to facility discretion.
educational_objective: Recognize that HIPAA generally gives individuals access to PHI in designated record sets and, when PHI is maintained electronically, a right to an electronic copy in a readily producible requested format, subject to limited denial grounds.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
source_document_title: Individuals’ Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information — 45 CFR §164.524
source_locator: 45 CFR §164.524(a), (c)(2)(ii); HHS guidance headings ‘General Right’ and ‘Under the HIPAA Privacy Rule, do individuals have the right to an electronic copy of their PHI?’
source_claim_supported: Individuals generally have a right to access PHI in designated record sets; if PHI is maintained electronically, they generally have a right to an electronic copy in the requested readily producible form and format, or an agreed readable alternative electronic format, subject to limited denial grounds.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; related activity statement: ‘Advocate for client rights and needs’
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — client rights and access to health information
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item to remove the unsupported implication that HIPAA guarantees access specifically through an online patient portal. The final item tests the actual federal right: access to PHI in a designated record set and, when maintained electronically, an electronic copy in a readily producible requested format subject to limited denial grounds.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: HIPAA right of access / electronic PHI
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current HHS/OCR right-of-access guidance and 45 CFR §164.524. HHS expressly distinguishes the legal right to an electronic copy from any particular portal mechanism.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The final stem is limited to PHI in a designated record set maintained electronically. The correct option tracks §164.524(c)(2)(ii) and preserves the limited-denial qualification in §164.524(a). No claim that a specific portal must be offered remains.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect. Paper cannot be substituted merely for staff convenience when the electronic-copy requirements apply and an electronic format is readily producible.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct. It states the electronic-copy right with the readily-producible and limited-denial qualifications.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect. HHS states that individuals exercising the HIPAA access right are not required to state their purpose.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect. HIPAA creates the access right; it is not wholly discretionary facility policy.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B accurately combines the access right, electronic format requirement, and legal limitations; A, C, and D each contradict HHS guidance.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are similar in scope and all concern the conditions of electronic access; the correct option is not signaled by grammar or an absolute-versus-qualified pattern alone.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is appropriate because the item tests client rights and nursing recognition of legally protected access.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited the reconstructed item for portal-versus-copy precision, designated-record-set scope, electronic form/format requirements, denial exceptions, purpose-of-request rules, distractor plausibility, second-answer risk, and NCLEX relevance. No unresolved conflict remained.
